title: Anchor receipts published a forward-looking execution-engine label as present-tense fact
summary: The anchor-receipt schema defined the optional anchor.chain_backend field on 2026-06-23, and the receipt generator wrote it as the unconditional literal "pulsevm" — an execution engine announced for Metal A-chain, not the stack observed serving it. Every artifact published from the first anchor onward carried that forward-looking label as present-tense fact: /api/anchor-receipt.json, both lines of /api/anchor-history.jsonl (the cycle 3 anchor of 2026-07-04 and the cycle 4 anchor of 2026-08-04) and the archived receipt at api/archive/anchor-receipt-32529f4aadee1ef9906fd6be5253ceb9ea9a5b8b76b55c0cf41770ec36eefc4c.json. The four synthetic schema examples served from the same path — /api/anchor-receipt.example.json, /api/anchor-receipt.v2.example.json, /api/anchor-receipt.phase-beta.example.json and /api/anchor-history.example.jsonl — carried the same value; they document field shape and describe no transaction, but they are published, so they are listed here too and were corrected in the same change. The transactions were and are served by an Antelope/EOSIO-family stack: the generator resolves them through Hyperion /v2/history/get_actions and /v1/history/get_transaction, and they consist of eosio.token::transfer actions authorized by actor@permission — exactly what the generator's own seven verification gates assert. Nothing else in those artifacts was affected: transaction ids, block numbers, memos, branch roots and dag_root_computed were correct throughout and remain independently verifiable on a public XPR explorer, so none of the integrity checks described in docs/IDENTITY_VERIFICATION.md returns a different result because of this. The correction has two distinct dates: the generator, the ledger writer, the schemas and the published examples were corrected in the repository on 2026-08-17; the corrected schemas and examples are served here no later than this record itself and can be checked directly, while the first receipt actually carrying the corrected value is the cycle 5 anchor of 2026-09-04 — no receipt is generated in between. The field is documented as the protocol family observed serving the chain rather than an execution engine, and a regression test pins the value. The ledger is append-only, so its two existing lines keep the label they were published with, and the cycle 4 archived receipt is content-addressed by transaction id and likewise keeps its published bytes: a holder of an earlier copy will still find "pulsevm" in both. One further reference remains in the project's governing document, which may be amended only by the operator; that wording is queued for amendment. No effect on validator operation, delegations, or recorded uptime was identified in the records reviewed.
